edits.reason: n8n workflows can contain loops; "DAG" is inaccurate

edits.find: n8n is built from the ground up as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) workflow engine. Published under a fair-code model (Sustainable Use License), n8n bridges the gap between no-code visual modeling and full-stack software development.
edits.replace: n8n is a node-based visual workflow engine that bridges the gap between no-code modeling and software development. Its source code is published under the Sustainable Use License, which n8n calls "fair-code": you may use and modify it for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use, and may distribute it only free of charge for non-commercial purposes. It is therefore not an OSI-approved open-source license, and files marked ".ee" (enterprise features) require a separate n8n Enterprise License. Agencies planning to host n8n for clients should read the license terms carefully.
edits.reason: License terms verified on GitHub and stated accurately

edits.find: Developers have full access to global variables, runtime memory, and external npm packages, allowing for sophisticated data transformations that would require third-party microservices on Zapier or Make.
edits.replace: On self-hosted instances, administrators can also allow external npm packages in the Code node, which makes some data transformations possible without a separate microservice.

edits.find: However, technical analysis indicates clear architectural trade-offs:
edits.replace: However, there are trade-offs to consider:

edits.find: • Absence of Native Vector Stores: While Zapier offers basic knowledge base uploads, it lacks native integration with production vector databases (such as Pinecone, Qdrant, or Weaviate) for enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
edits.replace: • Less RAG Plumbing: Zapier offers fewer building blocks for custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines than n8n's dedicated vector store nodes.

edits.find: • High Execution Overhead: Passing conversational turns through multi-step Zaps rapidly consumes task quotas, increasing operational expenses.
edits.replace: • Task Consumption: AI steps are billed in tasks, so multi-step agent runs can use up a plan's task allowance quickly.

edits.find: Make provides modular connectors for OpenAI (including GPT-4o and Assistants API), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.
edits.replace: Make provides modular connectors for major model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini.

edits.find: n8n is the clear architectural leader in autonomous AI workflow design. Rather than simply providing an API connector to an LLM endpoint, n8n integrates a native implementation of LangChain directly into its workflow canvas.
edits.replace: Of the three, n8n exposes the most AI-agent building blocks directly on its canvas. Rather than only providing an API connector to an LLM endpoint, n8n's AI nodes use LangChain's JavaScript framework.

edits.find: • AI Agent Nodes: Support ReAct (Reasoning + Acting), Conversational, and Plan-and-Execute agent architectures out of the box.
edits.replace: • AI Agent Node: Since n8n 1.82, the AI Agent node works as a "Tools Agent" that lets the model decide which connected tools to call; the older agent-type setting is deprecated.

edits.find: • Vector Store Nodes: Native, direct connections to Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase PGVector, Weaviate, Chroma, and In-Memory vector databases for scalable RAG pipelines.
edits.replace: • Vector Store Nodes: Dedicated nodes for vector databases such as Pinecone and Qdrant, plus an in-memory Simple Vector Store, for building RAG pipelines.

edits.find: running on private hardware, ensuring complete data containment.
edits.replace: running on private hardware, keeping prompts and data on your own infrastructure.

edits.find: n8n provides an enterprise-grade framework that rivals custom Python LangChain or LlamaIndex scripts, while preserving visual maintainability.
edits.replace: n8n can be a visual alternative to writing custom LangChain or LlamaIndex code for many use cases, although complex production systems still need engineering effort.

edits.find: Tasks (Zapier), Operations (Make), and Executions (n8n).
edits.replace: Tasks (Zapier), Credits (Make, formerly called operations), and Executions (n8n).

edits.find: • Make.com (Operation-Based): An "operation" is consumed every time any module performs an action, including routers, filters, tools, data stores, and webhooks. That same 4-action workflow in Make with a router and an iterator might consume 6 to 10 operations per run.
edits.replace: • Make.com (Credit-Based): According to Make's pricing page, "every time a module in a scenario performs an action, it consumes credits." Most actions cost one credit and some AI features cost more, while routers and error-handler modules do not consume credits. Scenarios that iterate over many items use credits for each item processed.
edits.reason: Corrected: routers do not consume; credits replaced operations; invented 6-10 figure removed

edits.find: • n8n Cloud (Execution-Based): An "execution" encompasses the entire run of a workflow
edits.replace: • n8n Cloud (Execution-Based): Per n8n's pricing page, an "execution" is a single run of your entire workflow

edits.find: • n8n Self-Hosted (Infrastructure-Based): When self-hosted on your own Virtual Private Server (VPS) or cloud cluster, there are zero per-execution fees. The only ongoing cost is your underlying server compute.
edits.replace: • n8n Self-Hosted (Infrastructure-Based): The self-hosted Community Edition does not charge per execution; your costs are the server, backups, security maintenance and your own time. Paid self-hosted Business and Enterprise plans add features and require a license key, and all self-hosted use is subject to the Sustainable Use License.

edits.replace: Because each platform counts usage differently, the cheapest option depends on how many steps your workflows have and how many items they process. As listed on the vendors' pricing pages in November 2026 (prices change; check the links before deciding):

edits.find: Note: Pricing figures are industry estimates based on published platform tiers and standard cloud VPS costs. Real-world expenses vary based on multi-step branching, payload sizes, compute requirements, and third-party API token expenditures.
edits.replace:
• Zapier: a Free plan with 100 tasks per month (two-step Zaps only); paid plans are priced by task volume, starting from $19.99 per month billed annually for 750 tasks on the Professional plan (Zapier pricing).
  • Make: a Free plan with 1,000 credits per month, plus paid Core, Pro, Teams and Enterprise tiers priced by credit volume (Make pricing).
  • n8n Cloud: Starter at €20 per month for 2,500 executions and Pro at €50 per month for 10,000 executions, both billed annually (n8n pricing). Self-hosting avoids execution fees but adds server and maintenance costs.

Note: We have not modelled exact monthly costs because they depend on step counts, items processed, AI usage and third-party API fees. Estimate your own volume with each vendor's pricing calculator before committing.
edits.reason: Invented cost-estimate table removed; replaced with verified plan facts

edits.find: Zapier quickly becomes cost-prohibitive. Make offers a dramatically more affordable cloud entry point for small-to-medium loads. For enterprise volume or agency operations handling hundreds of thousands of events, self-hosting n8n on high-performance VPS and cloud hosting infrastructure delivers unmatched cost efficiency.
edits.replace: Zapier's per-task billing can become expensive at high volumes. Make's credit model is often cheaper for complex multi-step scenarios. At very high volumes, self-hosting n8n (see our web hosting comparison for hosting basics) can cost the least, provided you have the skills to run, update and secure the server. Compare against your actual workflows rather than general rules.

edits.find: • Make.com: Does not feature a dedicated raw code execution node. While remarkably capable for manipulating data strings, writing complex algorithmic logic or processing raw binary files without external webhooks remains difficult.
edits.replace: • Make.com: Provides a comprehensive library of inline functions (math, string parsing, dates, regex, and array mapping). On paid plans, the Make Code app (in open beta as of November 2026) runs JavaScript or Python in a sandbox with CPU, memory and time limits, and bills credits per second of execution; custom libraries are Enterprise-only.
